name: Glomus Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Glomus Tumor

criteria.description: Presence of a small, localized, exquisitely tender subungual or subcutaneous nodule
Histopathological confirmation showing nests of glomus cells surrounding vascular channels
Imaging evidence (MRI or ultrasound) showing a well-circumscribed vascular lesion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of localized tenderness and cold sensitivity with histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Imaging is supportive but not mandatory if histopathology is available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Exquisite localized tenderness at tumor site
Paroxysmal pain episodes localized to subungual or subcutaneous nodule
searchTerms: sudden sharp pain in nail or skin lump
pain attacks in small finger or skin nodule

common.symptomName: Visible bluish or reddish discoloration of overlying skin
searchTerms: visible purplish or reddish skin patch
skin color changes with bluish or reddish tint

common.symptomName: Small palpable subungual or subcutaneous nodule
searchTerms: small lump under nail or skin
tiny bump beneath skin or nail
increased sensitivity to cold at lesion
cold causes discomfort at affected area

occasional.symptomName: Nail deformity or dystrophy overlying subungual tumors
searchTerms: nail changes or damage over tumor

occasional.symptomName: Paresthesia or numbness near tumor site
Mild swelling or edema at lesion site
Tenderness to palpation beyond tumor margins
searchTerms: pain when touching beyond tumor edges

imaging: MRI showing well-circumscribed, highly vascular lesion with low T1 and high T2 signal intensity
Ultrasound demonstrating hypoechoic vascular nodule with increased blood flow on Doppler
genetic: Rare familial cases linked to mutations in GLMN gene (glomulin)
other: Histopathology revealing nests of uniform glomus cells surrounding vascular channels
Immunohistochemistry positive for smooth muscle actin and vimentin

distinguishingFeatures: Typically present at birth or early childhood
Different imaging characteristics with less circumscription
Pain related to nerve injury or trauma
Different histopathology with nerve tissue proliferation

redFlags: Persistent severe pain unresponsive to analgesics
references: Enzinger FM, Weiss SW. Soft Tissue Tumors. 6th ed. Elsevier; 2014.
Schiefer TK, Parker WL, Anakwenze OA, Amadio PC, Inwards CY, Spinner RJ. Diagnosis and treatment of glomus tumor of the hand: a series of 51 cases. Mayo Clin Proc. 2006;81(7):932-6.
